I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and it gives me steadier grain output for the year. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10 mu, and I will keep 5 mu for cotton because I have grown it many years and it still gives me cash income, even though it takes more field management. Since some family members work off-farm, I will not choose the most labor-intensive way of farming. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, do medium fertilizer input, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and control pests enough to protect the crop but not spray too many times. For wheat and maize I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and saves labor compared with deep ploughing every time. For cotton I will also use rotary tillage and manage water and fertilizer more carefully, because too much input raises my cost. My goal this year is stable production first, with cotton bringing cash and wheat-maize securing the main harvest.
